intro: A finding is an actively exploited vulnerability (CISA KEV) that matches one of your devices. Confirmed means a safe scan template saw the vulnerability; suspected means it only matches by version or product.
caption: Findings list

versionNeeded.title_one: Add the version of 1 software to check it
versionNeeded.title_other: Add the version of {{count}} software to check them
versionNeeded.help: Vedette compares the version with the versions each exploited CVE affects. Without a version it cannot tell, so it lists the product here once instead of one finding per CVE. Open the device and add the version.
versionNeeded.missing_one: {{software}} has no version: adding it checks 1 exploited CVE.
versionNeeded.missing_other: {{software}} has no version: adding it checks {{count}} exploited CVEs.
versionNeeded.unreadable_one: {{software}} version "{{version}}" cannot be compared: enter it as numbers (for example 7.2.5) to check 1 exploited CVE.
versionNeeded.unreadable_other: {{software}} version "{{version}}" cannot be compared: enter it as numbers (for example 7.2.5) to check {{count}} exploited CVEs.

emptyCve: No findings for {{cve}} in this filter.
emptyHelp: Vedette only matches vulnerabilities against devices it knows. If you have no devices yet, add them first; once you do, run a scan to check right away. Vedette will tell you when a new vulnerability matches.

headline.confirmed: {{device}} has a confirmed vulnerability ({{cve}}) that is being exploited in the wild
headline.suspected: {{device}} may be affected by {{cve}}: needs checking
headline.mitigated: {{device}}: {{cve}} is mitigated, patching is still needed to remove it

device.title: Findings on this device
device.description: Exploited vulnerabilities that match this device.
device.none: No findings for this device yet.
device.handleAll: Select and handle these findings in the Findings list

status.title: Mark as handled
status.description: Record a new status for {{cve}}. History is kept so others know who changed it and why.
status.noteRequired: Say why this is a false positive or not relevant (at least 3 characters).
status.patchedHint: The vendor patch is installed. Rescan to confirm.
status.mitigatedHint: Not patched, but the way in is blocked (for example Internet access cut off).
status.false_positiveHint: The device is not affected; Vedette matched it wrongly.
status.not_relevantHint: Affected, but no action needed (for example a device being retired, not on the network).

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: Why Vedette thinks this device is affected, and how you can check it yourself.
evidence.none: No scan evidence for this finding yet.
evidence.noTemplate: No safe scan template for this CVE yet
evidence.noTemplateRun: A template exists; not yet run on this device
evidence.recheckCode: Run from a machine on the internal network
evidence.noIpScan: This device has no IP address in your inventory, so Vedette cannot scan it. Add its IP on the device page to scan it.

rec.title: What to do
rec.description: The source of a recommendation is always stated: confirmed by Vedette maintainers, or none yet.
rec.appliedHint: Only writes a log entry. The finding changes status after you mark it or rescan.
rec.confirmedBy: Confirmed by {{by}} on {{date}} through a GitHub pull request. Drafted with AI, every step checked by a maintainer.
rec.workaroundTitle: 2. Temporary workaround if you cannot update yet
rec.firewallTitle: 3. Firewall configuration to cut off access
rec.firewallHint: Each command is in its own box; paste them one at a time, in order. Read the side effects before pasting.
rec.fwDetected: Pre-selected the firewall vendor you declared in the inventory.
rec.fwNone: You have not declared a firewall in the inventory, so below is general guidance and reference syntax.
rec.checklistHint: Tick as you finish ({{done}}/{{total}}). Only for tracking on this screen; not saved.
rec.noPackBody: Vedette maintainers have not confirmed a step-by-step pack for this CVE yet. Below is everything this box knows: what CISA requires, where the vendor's fix is, and how to check your device. It is source information, not a Vedette recommendation. Your own AI can draft more; its answer always carries the AI-generated label.
rec.sourceHint: CISA's required action when it added this vulnerability on {{date}} (original English).
rec.dueDate: CISA's deadline for US federal agencies: {{date}}. Use it as your own deadline.
rec.ransomware: Ransomware groups have used this flaw, so handle it before the deadline.
rec.noFixedVersion: Vedette does not have the fixed version for this CVE yet. The vendor advisory says which version fixes it.
rec.noVendorLink: CISA lists no vendor link for this flaw. Search the vendor's security advisories for {{cve}} ({{product}}).
rec.step1: Find which version of {{product}} {{device}} runs, and add it to the device on the Devices page so Vedette can compare it.
rec.step2Due: If it is older than the fixed version in the advisory, update it by {{date}}.
rec.step2: If it is older than the fixed version in the advisory, update it.
rec.step3: Then mark this finding as Patched. If the version is already fixed, mark it as False positive and write the version in the note.
rec.noKev: This CVE is not on the CISA list this box holds, so there is no source information to show.

compromise.title: Have I been hit?
compromise.description: Signs that the device was exploited, and commands to check yourself.
compromise.none: No confirmed exploitation signs for this CVE yet. Follow the recheck steps under Evidence and look at the device logs around the day the vulnerability was published.

aside.label: Device and history
aside.noDevice: The device is no longer in the inventory.

explain.title: Explain in plain language
explain.description: Your AI explains whether this device is affected and why.

ai.unavailable: The AI assistant is off, or no AI profile is assigned to this job.
ai.privacy: Sent to the AI provider you configured, with your key. Data level is set in Settings, AI assistant.

risk.unverifiedHint: Unverified: product match only. Vedette knows the product but not its version, so this may not apply to you. Add the version on the device page, or run a scan, to check.
risk.unverifiedLine: Unverified: product match only. The severity applies only if the version on this device is affected.

bulk.tooMany: At most {{max}} at a time. Narrow the filter.
bulk.description: One status and one note for every selected open finding. Findings already closed keep their status and note. Each finding keeps its own history line, so others can see who changed it and why.
bulk.noteHint: The same note is saved on each finding.
bulk.skipped_one: {{count}} was already closed and kept its status.
bulk.skipped_other: {{count}} were already closed and kept their status.
